summary: Wizard (FS.GG.NewSddWorkspace) 0.12.0 through 0.21.0 selected typed-sdd for an omitted fable-game lifecycle only when the fetched descriptor's source was exactly FS.GG.Workspace.Template::0.15.0, and always forwarded an explicit lifecycle=<token> to fsgg-sdd scaffold. Once Templates moved the pin, omitted Wizard creation recorded sdd while direct and provider routes recorded the descriptor default typed-sdd, losing the D.5 default (FS-GG/.github#4811). Tagged fable-game descriptors from 0.9.0 declare their own omission default: sdd through 0.14.0, typed-sdd from 0.15.0 (cited at 0.14.0, 0.15.0 and 0.19.3); 0.8.x declare none, so the Wizard keeps sdd. The #4811 source fix reads the lifecycle parameter's declared default from the fetched descriptor for fable-game only. Other templates keep the Wizard's sdd default, because pinned preflight runs before the fetch and treats only an omitted fable-game lifecycle as possibly typed. An explicit --lifecycle is unchanged; an absent or unrecognized declaration keeps sdd with a visible warning. A version-pinned behaviour switch silently expires when the pin advances, so prefer the provider's own declaration. Source delivery does not publish Wizard 0.22.0, and public qualification of omitted Wizard typed-sdd needs that publication plus the Templates verifier flip.
title: Wizard omitted fable-game lifecycle must follow the descriptor's declared default, not a version pin
